cues.zh: 我们生活的世界显得如此正常、普通。
cues.en: The world we live in feels normal, ordinary.

cues.zh: 让人觉得人类一直以来就是这样生存的。
cues.en: It feels like this is just how humans exist and always existed.

cues.zh: 但事实并非如此。
cues.en: But, it's not.

cues.zh: 人类从未生活在一个像今天这样先进、且完全契合我们需求的世界里。
cues.en: Never before have we humans lived in a world as sophisticated and engineered to our needs as today.

cues.zh: 让我们能够奢侈地忘却自我，不再为生存发愁。
cues.en: Giving us the luxury to forget about ourselves and not worry about survival.

cues.zh: 食物、居所、安全——这一切或多或少都被视作理所当然。
cues.en: Food, shelter, security – all of this is, more or less, taken for granted.

cues.zh: 但我们只是极少数的幸运儿；在超过 99.99% 的人类历史中，生活完全是另一番模样。
cues.en: But we're a special few; for more than 99.99% of human history, life was completely different.

cues.zh: 而且，人类的历史从来就不止一种。
cues.en: And there's no such thing as just one human history.

cues.zh: 我们的故事始于 600 万年前，当时人族分化，我们与猿类的亲缘关系就此终结。
cues.en: Our story begins 6 million years ago, when the tribe of hominini split and our relationship with the apes ended.

cues.zh: 280 万年前，人属——也就是最早的人类——诞生了。
cues.en: 2.8 million years ago, the genus of homo, the first humans, emerged.

cues.zh: 我们总习惯将自己视作唯一的人类，但这远非事实。
cues.en: We like to think about ourselves as the only humans, but this is far from the truth.

cues.zh: 20万年前，当我们智人出现时，地球上至少还存在其他六种人类。
cues.en: When we, homo sapiens sapiens, came into existence 200,000 years ago, there were at least six other human species around.

cues.zh: 这些表亲拥有相当的智力和能力，这肯定非常吓人，有点像和外星人生活在一起。
cues.en: Cousins of comparable intelligence and ability, which must have been incredibly scary, kind of like living with aliens.

cues.zh: 他们当中有些非常成功。
cues.en: Some of them were very successful.

cues.zh: 比如直立人，生存了200万年。
cues.en: Homo erectus, for example, survived for 2 million years.

cues.zh: 比现代人类存在的时间长了十倍。
cues.en: Ten times longer than modern humans have existed.

cues.zh: 其他最后的人类大约在1万年前消失。
cues.en: The last of the other humans disappeared around 10,000 years ago.

cues.zh: 我们不知道导致他们灭绝的原因。
cues.en: We don't know what caused them to die out.

cues.zh: 现代人类体内至少有百分之几的尼安德特人和其他人种的DNA，所以当时存在一些交融，
cues.en: Modern humans have at least a few percent of neanderthal and other human DNA, so there was some mixing,

cues.zh: 但显然不足以构成物种间的融合。
cues.en: but certainly not enough to be a merger between species.

cues.zh: 因此我们无从得知，这些表亲的消亡究竟是因为在资源竞争中落败，还是源于一系列小规模的种族屠杀。
cues.en: So we don't know if our cousins went away because they lost the battle over resources, or because of a series of minor genocides.

cues.zh: 无论如何，最后只剩下我们。
cues.en: Either way, only we remain.

cues.zh: 回到人类的起源。
cues.en: Back to the beginnings of humanity.

cues.zh: 280万年前，早期人类开始使用工具，但在近200万年里几乎没有什么进步。
cues.en: 2.8 million years ago, early humans used tools, but did not make a lot of progress for nearly 2 million years.

cues.zh: 直到他们学会了控制火。
cues.en: Until they learned to control fire.

cues.zh: 火让人类能够烹饪食物，让食物更有营养，也推动了我们的大脑发育。
cues.en: Fire meant cooking, which made food more nutritious, which contributed to the development of our brain.

cues.zh: 火还能提供光和热，让白天变得更长，也让冬天不再那么难熬。
cues.en: It also produced light and warmth, which made days longer and winters less gruesome.

cues.zh: 除此之外，火不仅能吓走捕食者，还能用来狩猎。
cues.en: On top of that, it not only scared predators away, it could also be used for hunting.

cues.zh: 烧过的树林或草地上，有预先烤熟的小动物、坚果和块茎。
cues.en: A torched wood or grassland provided small animals, nuts and tubers that were pre-roasted.

cues.zh: 从30万年前开始，大多数不同的人类物种都生活在小型狩猎采集社群中。
cues.en: From 300,000 years ago, most of the different human species lived in small hunter-gatherer societies.

cues.zh: 他们会用火，也会制作木器和石器；他们会为未来做打算，会埋葬死者，也有自己的文化。
cues.en: They had fire, wood and stone tools, planned for the future, buried their dead, and had cultures of their own.

cues.zh: 但最重要的是，他们会彼此交谈。
cues.en: But most importantly, they spoke to each other.

cues.zh: 大概会用一种原始语言，没我们的语言复杂。
cues.en: Probably in a kind of proto-language, less complex than ours.

cues.zh: 如果我们有一台时光机，能回到多远的过去，
cues.en: If we had a time machine, how far would we be able to go back,

cues.zh: 偷几个婴儿带到今天抚养，还不让人发现他们有点不一样？
cues.en: steal a few babies and raise them today without anyone noticing that they're a bit different?

cues.zh: 对此争论很多。
cues.en: There is much debate.

cues.zh: 从解剖学上看，现代人类在20万年前出现，
cues.en: Anatomically, modern humans emerged 200,000 years ago,

cues.zh: 但我们大概最多只能回到7万年前，抓到一个行为上已具备现代人特征的人类婴儿。
cues.en: but probably 70,000 years is as far as we could travel back and still snatch a behaviourally modern human.

cues.zh: 再早一些，婴儿可能还缺少几种关键的基因突变，
cues.en: Before that, the babies would probably lack a few crucial gene mutations

cues.zh: 而这些突变对大脑具备现代语言和抽象思维能力至关重要。
cues.en: Necessary to build a brain with modern language and abstract thinking abilities.

cues.zh: 大约5万年前，创新突然蓬勃发展。
cues.en: At some point, around 50,000 years ago, there was an explosion in innovation.

cues.zh: 工具和武器变得更加精巧，文化也更加复杂，
cues.en: Tools and weapons became more sophisticated and culture became more complex,

cues.zh: 因为那时，人类拥有了一颗多用途的大脑，
cues.en: because at this point, humans had a multi-purpose brain,

cues.zh: 也拥有了更先进的语言，能有效地彼此传递信息，
cues.en: and a more advanced language to communicate information with each other effectively,

cues.zh: 还能讲清每一个细节。
cues.en: and down to the last detail.

cues.zh: 这让合作更紧密，也正是这一点让我们与地球上其他生物截然不同。
cues.en: This allowed much closer cooperation, and is what really makes us different from any other creature on Earth.

cues.zh: 不是我们相对孱弱的身体和迟钝的感官，
cues.en: Not our comparatively weak bodies and inferior senses,

cues.zh: 而是能在大型群体中灵活合作的能力，不像僵化的蜂巢，
cues.en: but the ability to cooperate flexibly in large groups, unlike, for example, rigid beehives

cues.zh: 也不像亲密但规模很小的狼群。
cues.en: or intimate, but tiny wolf packs.

cues.zh: 随着大脑进化，我们开始能做到在此之前生命从未做到的事。
cues.en: As our brain evolved, we became able to do something, life had been unable to do up to this point.

cues.zh: 第一，快速扩展知识。
cues.en: One – expand knowledge quickly.

cues.zh: 第二，把获得的 knowledge 代代保存下来。
cues.en: Two – preserve the knowledge gained over generations.

cues.zh: 第三，在已有知识上继续积累，获得更深刻的洞见。
cues.en: Three – build on past knowledge, to gain even deeper insight.

cues.zh: 这听起来很傻，但在那之前，信息只能代代相传，
cues.en: This seems daft, but until then, information had to be passed on from generation to generation,

cues.zh: 主要通过遗传，而这种方式效率不高。
cues.en: mostly through genetics, which is not efficient.

cues.zh: 不过，在接下来的四万年里，人类生活基本没有太大变化。
cues.en: Still, for the next 40,000 years, human life remained more or less the same.

cues.zh: 几乎没有任何基础可言。
cues.en: There was little to build upon.

cues.zh: 我们的祖先不过是众多动物中的一种。
cues.en: Our ancestors were only one animal among many.

cues.zh: 在连房子是什么都不知道的情况下造摩天大楼……太难了。
cues.en: Building a skyscraper without knowing what a house is… is hard.

cues.zh: 我们很容易以傲慢的态度看待祖先，但这其实是一种无知。
cues.en: But while it is easy to be arrogant in our attitude to our ancestors, this would be ignorant.

cues.zh: 五万年前的人类都是生存专家。
cues.en: Humans 50,000 years ago were survival specialists.

cues.zh: 他们对自己的领地了如指掌，
cues.en: They had a detailed mental map of their territory,

cues.zh: 他们的感官敏锐地适应着周围环境，
cues.en: their senses were fine-tuned to the environment,

cues.zh: 他们掌握并记住了海量的动植物信息。
cues.en: they knew and memorized a great amount of information about plants and animals.

cues.zh: 他们能制作复杂的工具，这需要多年的严苛训练和极精细的动作技能，
cues.en: They could make complicated tools that required years of careful training and very fine motor skills

cues.zh: 仅凭日常生活，他们的体魄就能媲美今天的运动员，
cues.en: Their bodies compared to our athletes today just because of their daily routines,

cues.zh: 而且他们在部落内拥有丰富的社交生活。
cues.en: and they lived a rich social life within their tribe

cues.zh: 生存所需的技能如此之多，以至于早期现代人的平均脑容量
cues.en: Survival required so many skills that the average brain volume of early modern humans

cues.zh: 甚至可能比今天还要大。
cues.en: might even have been bigger than it is today

cues.zh: 作为一个群体，我们今天所知更多；但作为个体，我们的祖先比我们更强。
cues.en: As a group we know more today, but as individuals our ancestors were superior to us

cues.zh: 然而大约在一万两千年前，人类在多地发展出了农业。
cues.en: But then around 12,000 years ago, in multiple locations, humans developed agriculture.

cues.zh: 一切变化得非常之快。
cues.en: Everything changed very quickly.

cues.zh: 在此之前，作为狩猎采集者生存，需要每个人在各个方面都拥有极佳的体能和心智。
cues.en: Before, survival as a hunter and forager required superb physical and mental abilities in all fields from everybody

cues.zh: 随着农业时代的兴起，个体越来越能依靠他人的技能来生存。
cues.en: With the rise of the agricultural age, individuals could increasingly rely on the skills of others for survival.

cues.zh: 这意味着他们中的一部分人可以走向专业化。
cues.en: This meant that some of them could specialize.

cues.zh: 也许他们去改进工具，也许他们花时间培育抗病性更强的作物或更优良的牲畜，
cues.en: Maybe they worked on better tools, maybe they took time to breed more resistant crops or better livestock,

cues.zh: 也许他们开始搞发明创造。
cues.en: Maybe they started inventing things.

cues.zh: 随着农耕效率的不断提高，我们所谓的文明拉开了序幕。
cues.en: As farming got more and more efficient, what we call civilization began

cues.zh: 农业为我们提供了可靠且可预期的食物来源，
cues.en: Agriculture gave us a reliable and predictable food source,

cues.zh: 这让人类首次得以大规模储备粮食，
cues.en: which allowed humans to hoard food on a large scale for the first time,

cues.zh: 毕竟储存谷物比储存肉类容易得多，
cues.en: which is much easier to do with grains than meat,

cues.zh: 储备的食物需要保护，这促使社群在更紧凑的空间内聚居，
cues.en: The food stock required protection, which led to communities living together in tighter spaces

cues.zh: 首先，早期的防御设施被建立起来，组织协调的需求也随之增长。
cues.en: First, early defense structures were built, the need for organization grew

cues.zh: 我们的组织化程度越高，事情变得高效的速度就越快。
cues.en: The more organized we got, the faster things became efficient

cues.zh: 村落演变成城市，城市演变成王国，王国演变成帝国。
cues.en: Villages became cities, cities became kingdoms, kingdoms became empires

cues.zh: 人与人之间的连接呈爆炸式增长，从而带来了交流知识的契机。
cues.en: Connections between humans exploded which led to opportunities to exchange knowledge

cues.zh: 进步呈现出指数级增长。
cues.en: Progress became exponential

cues.zh: 大约 500 年前，科学革命爆发了。
cues.en: About 500 years ago the Scientific Revolution began

cues.zh: 数学、物理学、天文学、生物学和化学，彻底颠覆了我们自以为认知的一切。
cues.en: Mathematics, Physics, Astronomy, Biology, and Chemistry transformed everything we thought we knew

cues.zh: 紧随其后的工业革命，则为现代世界奠定了基石。
cues.en: The Industrial Revolution followed soon after laying the foundation for the modern world

cues.zh: 随着整体效率指数级增长，
cues.en: As our overall efficiency grew exponentially,

cues.zh: 更多人能毕生为人类进步做贡献
cues.en: more people could spend their lifetime contributing to the progress of humanity

cues.zh: 革命不断发生。
cues.en: Revolutions kept happening.

cues.zh: 计算机的发明，及其演变为我们日常使用的媒介，
cues.en: The invention of the computer, its evolution into a medium we all use on a daily basis,

cues.zh: 还有互联网的兴起，塑造了我们的世界
cues.en: and the rise of the Internet shaped our world

cues.zh: 很难想象这一切发生得有多快
cues.en: It's hard to grasp how fast all of that happened

cues.zh: 自首个原始人类物种出现，大约已过12.5万代
cues.en: It's been about 125,000 generations since the emergence of the first human species

cues.zh: 约7500代前，生理上的现代人诞生
cues.en: About 7,500 generations since the physiologically modern humans saw the light of day

cues.zh: 500代前，我们所谓的文明开始了
cues.en: 500 generations ago, what we call civilization began

cues.zh: 20代前，我们学会了怎么做科学
cues.en: 20 generations ago, we learned how to do science

cues.zh: 而互联网向大多数人开放，仅是上一代人的事
cues.en: And the Internet became available to most people only one generation ago

cues.zh: 今天我们生活在人类史上最繁荣的时代
cues.en: Today we live in the most prosperous age humanity has ever experienced

cues.zh: 我们改变了这颗星球，从大气构成到地貌的大规模变化
cues.en: We have transformed this planet, from the composition of its atmosphere to large-scale changes in its landscape

cues.zh: 以及其他现存动物的处境。
cues.en: and also in terms of the other animals in existence.

cues.zh: 我们用人造星星点亮夜空，把人送进天空中的金属盒子
cues.en: We light up the night with artificial stars and put people in a metal box in the sky

cues.zh: 有些人甚至还在月球上行走过
cues.en: Some have even walked on our Moon

cues.zh: 我们把机器人送上其他星球
cues.en: We put robots on other planets

cues.zh: 我们用机械之眼，深入探寻宇宙的过去
cues.en: We've looked deep into the past of the universe with mechanical eyes

cues.zh: 我们的知识，以及获取和储存更多知识的能力，都飞速增长
cues.en: Our knowledge and our way of acquiring and storing more of it has exploded

cues.zh: 如今的普通高中生，对宇宙的了解超过了几百年前的学者
cues.en: The average high school student today knows more about the universe than a scholar a few centuries ago

cues.zh: 人类主宰着这颗星球，尽管我们的统治十分脆弱
cues.en: Humans dominate this planet, even if our rule is very fragile

cues.zh: 我们和七万年前的祖先仍没那么不同
cues.en: We are still not that different from our ancestors 70,000 years ago

cues.zh: 但你现在的生活方式，在人类历史中存在的时间还不到 0.001%
cues.en: But your lifestyle has existed for less than 0.001% of human history

cues.zh: 从现在起，未来会怎样，没人说得准
cues.en: From here on, there's no saying what the future holds for us

cues.zh: 我们正在建造一座摩天大楼，却不确定它是否立在坚实的地基上
cues.en: We're building a skyscraper, but we're not sure if it's standing on a solid foundation

cues.zh: 还是建在流沙上
cues.en: or if we're building it on quicksand

cues.zh: 我们暂且就说到这里
cues.en: Let's leave it with that for now

cues.zh: 下次你赶不上火车、汉堡不够热，或者有人插队时
cues.en: The next time you miss your train, your burger is not hot enough, or someone cuts in line

cues.zh: 想想这个人造世界有多么特别
cues.en: Remember how special this made-up human world is

cues.zh: 也许没必要为这些琐事烦恼。
cues.en: Maybe it's not worth being upset about all those little things.

cues.zh: 好，这就是我们制作历史类视频的初次尝试
cues.en: OK, so this was our first take on making a history-related video

cues.zh: 我们很想多做一些，但它们比一般的视频还要耗时得多。
cues.en: we'd love to make much more of them, but they take even more time than our average video.

cues.zh: 所以我们大概一年做个三四期。
cues.en: So we might do 3 or 4 a year.

cues.zh: 非常欢迎大家提出反馈
cues.en: Your feedback's very welcome here

cues.zh: 非常感谢大家的观看，如果你想直接支持我们，
cues.en: Thank you so much for watching, and if you want to support us directly,

cues.zh: 可以在 Patreon 上赞助。
cues.en: you can do so on Patreon.

cues.zh: 这真的对我们帮助很大。
cues.en: It really helps us out.

cues.zh: 在你考虑的同时，如果你想找点别的消遣，这里还有更多视频。
cues.en: While you think about it, here are more videos, if you need more distraction.
